doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

chapter: Richmond and arriving in New York
title: Competitiveness at jam sessions
summary: He did not find sessions hostile and valued being around better players.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Was there any — I’m not sure what word to use — competitiveness or even unpleasant atmosphere in some of those sessions, like people trying to make you look foolish?

You know I didn’t experience that. I had heard of certain sessions or certain people that could be that way but I didn’t experience that particularly. One thing, it was very healthy that you were around great players who either had more ability or more knowledge, and so I saw it as very healthy because it was a reference of what one needed to go home and work on. So yeah, I certainly got my behind kicked many times in jam sessions and probably still would, still do. There’s a lot I don’t know. But that’s the healthy part of music. That’s what keeps us humble. That’s what keeps us growing. We never know it all.
